--- name: javaifcheck description: Branches a scenario on a programmatic (Java) condition. ---
# Programmatic If Check
Branches a scenario on a programmatic (Java) condition.
## When to use
- A scenario must choose its next step from a fixed rule rather than an LLM decision.
## How it works
1. Meant to evaluate a condition and run only the child steps whose branch matches.
## Inputs
None. It does not read any values from the agent context.
## Notes
- No Spring bean named `javaLogicAgent` is registered in plugin.xml, so this skill cannot run yet.
## Implementation
- Bean `javaLogicAgent`: not registered - Agent type: `logicagent`

--- name: toolifcheck description: Branches a scenario by asking the LLM which child step to run and with which arguments. ---
# LLm If Check
Branches a scenario by asking the LLM which child step to run and with which arguments.
## When to use
- The next step depends on understanding free text, such as routing an email or chat message.
## How it works
1. Meant to work like ToolsCallingSkill: each child step's `parameterstructure` becomes a tool definition. 2. With one child, the LLM (`agentparams`) fills in its parameters. With several, the LLM (`agentdecision`) picks one. 3. The chosen child runs with the arguments the LLM returned.
## Inputs
None. It does not read any values from the agent context.
## Notes
- No Spring bean named `llmToolAgent` is registered in plugin.xml, so this skill cannot run yet. The closest implementation is `ToolsCallingSkill`.
## Implementation
- Bean `llmToolAgent`: not registered - Agent type: `logicagent`

--- name: copyWebRequest description: Copies parameters, user profile and session values from the current web request into the agent context. ---
# Handle Web Request
Copies parameters, user profile and session values from the current web request into the agent context.
## When to use
- A scenario started from a web page needs the request values available to later steps.
## How it works
1. Meant to copy the request's parameters and user into the context. `handleWebEventSkill` does this today.
## Inputs
None. It does not read any values from the agent context.
## Notes
- No Spring bean named `copyWebRequestAgent` is registered in plugin.xml, so this skill cannot run yet. The closest implementation is `HandleWebEventSkill (bean handleWebEventSkill)`.
## Implementation
- Bean `copyWebRequestAgent`: not registered - Agent type: `eventagent`

--- name: runEventSkill description: Runs a catalog path event (/<catalogid>/events/<runoperation>.html) in the current thread and waits for it to finish. ---
# Run Event
Runs a catalog path event (`/<catalogid>/events/<runoperation>.html`) in the current thread and waits for it to finish.
## When to use
- A scenario needs to run an existing path event as one of its steps, with the agent context available to it.
## How it works
1. Reads `runoperation` from this skill row. 2. Copies the `webpagerequest` from the context into a new request and puts the agent context on it as `currentagentcontext`. 3. Runs the event through PathEventManager and blocks until it finishes, then runs the child steps.
## Inputs
- `webpagerequest`: The web request whose parameters and user are passed to the event
## Configuration
Attributes set on this skill row:
- `runoperation`: Event path relative to the catalog's `events` folder, e.g. `conversions/runconversions`
## Outputs
- Whatever the event's actions or scripts produce. `webpagerequest` is replaced with the request the event ran with
## Implementation
- Bean `runEventSkill`: `org.entermediadb.ai.skills.RunEventSkill` - Agent type: `eventagent`

--- name: runSharedEventSkill description: Queues a catalog path event to run in the background, at most one copy at a time. ---
# Run Event In Thread
Queues a catalog path event to run in the background, at most one copy at a time.
## When to use
- The event is long-running or may be triggered often, and the scenario should not wait for it.
## How it works
1. Reads `runoperation` from this skill row. 2. Calls `runSharedPathEvent`. If the same event is already queued or running it is flagged to run again soon instead of starting a second copy. 3. Runs the child steps right away without waiting for the event.
## Inputs
None. It does not read any values from the agent context.
## Configuration
Attributes set on this skill row:
- `runoperation`: Event path relative to the catalog's `events` folder, e.g. `publishing/publishassets`
## Outputs
- Whatever the event's actions or scripts produce, later in the background
## Notes
- The event does not receive the agent context or the web request.
## Implementation
- Bean `runSharedEventSkill`: `org.entermediadb.ai.skills.RunSharedEventSkill` - Agent type: `eventagent`

--- name: runModuleSkill description: Calls a module action (Module.method) directly through the ModuleManager. ---
# Run Module Event
Calls a module action (`Module.method`) directly through the ModuleManager.
## When to use
- A scenario step should run one module method rather than a whole path event.
## How it works
1. Reads `runoperation` from this skill row and replaces the first `_` with `.`, so `EntityModule_handleAssetsImported` also works. 2. Calls `ModuleManager.execute(operation, webpagerequest)`, then runs the child steps.
## Inputs
- `webpagerequest`: The web request passed to the module method
## Configuration
Attributes set on this skill row:
- `runoperation`: The module action to call, e.g. `EntityModule.handleAssetsImported`
## Outputs
- Whatever the module method puts on the request or saves
## Implementation
- Bean `runModuleSkill`: `org.entermediadb.ai.skills.RunModuleSkill` - Agent type: `eventagent`

--- name: handleWebEventSkill description: Copies an incoming web request into the agent context and optionally jumps to a named automation step. ---
# Handle Web Event
Copies an incoming web request into the agent context and optionally jumps to a named automation step.
## When to use
- First step of a scenario that is started from a web page or form post.
## How it works
1. Copies every request parameter into the context. 2. If no entity is set yet and `entitymoduleid` is posted, loads the entity and module and sets them as the current entity. 3. Sets `triggersiteroot`, the user profile, and `nextautomationstep` from the request. 4. If `nextautomationstep` is set, runs that step directly. Otherwise runs the child steps.
## Inputs
- `webpagerequest`: The incoming web request - `entitymoduleid`: Request parameter: module id of the entity to work on - `entityid`: Request parameter: id of the entity to work on - `nextautomationstep`: Request parameter: id of the automation step to jump to
## Outputs
- All request parameters, `triggersiteroot`, the current entity and module, and the user profile in the context
## Implementation
- Bean `handleWebEventSkill`: `org.entermediadb.ai.skills.HandleWebEventSkill` - Agent type: `eventagent`
